title: Emission stalls + KV-warmup playbook (micro-investigations)
content:
Purpose:
This is a focused, lightweight playbook for reproducing and mitigating intermittent emission stalls that show up as p99 spikes in end-to-end traces. The pattern we saw in production: steady p50/p95, but bursts of 200–800ms extra latency concentrated in the emit/response-assembly stages when certain request shapes hit cold KV caches and interact poorly with the async batcher handoff.

Scope / when to use:
- Use when p99 >> p95 and the waterfall shows most extra time after model token generation (emit/egress).
- Useful for regressions that only appear at certain sequence-length distributions or with certain prompt prefixes (long context + short reply).

High-level hypothesis (summary):
1) KV-cache miss during prefix reconstruction triggers synchronous KV population which stalls model-side emission loop.
2) Async batcher handoff can queue emit tokens behind another worker waiting on external IO, causing microblocking.
3) Small-batch model kernels are sensitive to jitter: a single blocking syscall or NVLink stall propagates to the emission stage and causes p99 tail.

Quick triage checklist (order matters):
1) Confirm p50/p95/p99 across routes and sequence-length cohorts. Generate trace cohorts: short prompt (<=128), mid (129–1024), long (>1024).
2) Look at per-stage percentiles for: tokenization, prefix-assembly, kv-lookup, model-forward, emit, egress. If emit is where p99 rises, continue.
3) Grab full trace TL;DR: span timings + metadata (route, model, seq_len, batching_id, worker_id, node).
4) Correlate with KV miss rate for the same time window.
5) Check batcher queue lengths and handoff latencies (handshake span between batcher->worker).

Instrumentation additions to help reproduce: (short snippets you can apply quickly)
- Add a tag on traces: kv_warmup=true for requests that had any kv-miss in prefix reconstruction.
- Incremental debug counter: emit_stall_detected if time_between_last_model_emit_and_first_byte_sent > 20ms.
- Emit per-token micro-spans: emit-start/emit-end (only enabled under debug sampling to limit overhead).

Reproduction experiment (local / dev cluster):
1) Testbed config: 1x small worker, 1x batching proxy, synthetic load generator (ab) to control concurrency, seed KV store with partial prefix coverage so ~30% requests cold-miss.
2) Workloads: a) high qps small prompts (to exercise batching), b) sparse cold prefix requests (to force kv misses), c) blended 70/30 mix.
3) Metrics to collect: p50/p95/p99 per stage, kv miss rate, batcher_handshake_ms distribution, worker cpu/gpu utilization, NVLink error/jitter counters if available.
4) Run 10-minute steady windows and capture full traces for the highest p99 samples.

Representative trace excerpts (anonymized) — micro waterfall (times in ms)
Trace A (p95-ish):
- tokenize: 2
- prefix-assembly: 3
- kv-lookup: 1 (cache hit)
- model-forward (first chunk): 20
- emit (tokens 1..N): 10
- egress: 2
Total: ~38ms

Trace B (p99 spike, observed):
- tokenize: 2
- prefix-assembly: 6
- kv-lookup: 92 (synchronous population + disk read)
- model-forward (first chunk): 22
- emit (stall observed): 420 (emit loop blocked; interleaved handoff wait)
- egress: 2
Total: ~544ms
Notes: kv-lookup and emit strongly overlap in causality: population triggers blocking syscall which is visible as a long kv-lookup span, but the emit-stage swipe shows the bulk of the latency due to worker side backpressure.

Quantiles we repeatedly saw in affected routes (example window):
- p50 end-to-end: 42ms
- p95 end-to-end: 68ms
- p99 end-to-end: 520ms
Per-stage p99 (same window):
- kv-lookup p99: 240ms
- emit p99: 410ms
- model-forward p99: 40ms

Immediate mitigations (fast, low-risk):
- Defer synchronous KV population: allow the model to start emitting using a partial prefix while background populates cache. This converts a blocking kv lookup into a background memfill.
- Limit max synchronous KV read time: timebox kv reads (e.g., 50–100ms), return partial and schedule async fill.
- Batcher handshake timeout: if worker handshake takes >30ms, drop to a degraded path that avoids cross-worker waits.
- Increase debug sampling to capture emit micro-spans during the next incident window.

Medium-term engineering fixes (requires design work):
- Implement non-blocking prefix reconstruction: stream prefix tokens as they become available rather than atomic reconstruct.
- Ensure async-batcher handoff avoids priority inversion: handshake should be fast-path and not wait on IO that the worker will do later.
- Prefetch hot KV keys during onboarding or cold-start for known heavy routes.
- Add small jitter to async IO retries to avoid synchronized retry storms.

Evaluation plan to validate fixes:
1) Canary rollout: target 5% of traffic on the route with injected partial-kv misses to stress path. Observe p99 and per-stage p99 for 2 hours.
2) A/B test: baseline vs deferred-kv population. Measure: p99 end-to-end, kv-miss durability (error rates), failure modes on partial prefixes.
3) Safety checks: ensure partial prefixes don't degrade output quality beyond acceptable thresholds—run automated evals (BLEU/ROUGE or model-specific evaluator) on a sampled prompt set.

Runbook for oncall (short actionable steps):
- Alert triggers: p99 > 300ms for >5m and emit-stage p99 contributes >60% of the tail.
- Quick action: toggle deferred-kv-population flag (experimental) for affected route; notify SRE and product owners.
- Capture: save 200 full traces with emit micro-spans and attach to incident ticket.
- Rollback: revert flag if downstream quality regressions reported.

Notes & unresolved questions:
- We saw a small subset of worker types (cpu-bound vs gpu-bound) more impacted—need to map worker kernel scheduling to p99 spikes.
- NVLink telemetry correlated with a handful of traces; is there a hardware coupling with long KV reads? follow up with infra team.

Next steps (owners):
- (Evelyn) Run repro on dev cluster with explicit prefilling and post results by 2025-02-20.
- (Marco) Add emit micro-span sampling to prod traces and bump debug sampling to 0.5% for 24h (JIRA-RT-1248).
- (Samir) Prototype deferred-kv-population flag and small canary for one route.
- (Ava) Run output-quality checks for partial-prefix responses (eval harness).

Appendix: quick grep queries and debug commands
- Find traces with large emit spans: 
  tracer.query("span.name=emit AND span.duration_ms>200")
- Correlate kv misses: 
  metric.query("kv_cache.miss_rate{route=\"/complete\"}", window=1h)
- Local repro run: 
  ./scripts/repro/run_local.sh --kv-cold-rate=0.3 --qps=50 --duration=600 --capture-traces

This doc is intentionally concise and operational — the goal is to get a reliable repro and a low-risk mitigation in prod within a short timeframe.
